title: That they may all be one (John 17:20–26)
hook: he prays for all who will believe, that they may be one

segments.voice: Yesterday, he prayed for his friends to be guarded, not removed. Your line was in the world, but not of it. Did you send that message? Day six hundred forty-one.
screen: `IN THE WORLD, BUT NOT OF IT.`

segments.voice: Up to now, Jesus has been praying for the people at the table. Eleven men, tired and confused, a few hours before the worst night of their lives. Then the prayer widens. He looks past the room, past that night, past the century, and prays for people who haven't been born yet. Christians hear themselves in this line. If you've ever been in a church, or a choir, or a Bible study, or anywhere people pray in his name, this is the moment Christians say he prayed for you.

In the King James Bible: "Neither pray I for these alone, but for them also which shall believe on me through their word; That they all may be one; as thou, Father, art in me, and I in thee, that they also may be one in us: that the world may believe that thou hast sent me." Look at the shape of that. The model for oneness is not an organization. It's the bond between the Father and the Son: you in me, and I in you. And the purpose is outward: that the world may believe. The way Christians treat each other is meant to say something to everyone watching. Here's the honest part. Christians have not always lived this prayer. Churches of the East and West parted ways. The Reformation brought more divisions. Today there are a great many separate church bodies, and Christians in many of them name that as a real grief. This verse has also been a seed. In more recent times, churches that had long been apart began talking, praying together, and in some cases reuniting. That movement is often called ecumenism. When Pope John Paul the Second wrote a letter on Christian unity in 1995, he titled it with this verse in Latin: Ut unum sint, that they may be one. Protestant and Orthodox voices for unity quote it too. Churches still differ, honestly, on what that unity should look like: one visible church, or many churches recognizing each other, or a shared life in the Spirit across different names. The prayer itself doesn't spell it out.
screen: `ONE, AS THE FATHER AND SON ARE ONE.`
`UT UNUM SINT: A SEED FOR UNITY.`
then, large: `THAT THEY ALL MAY BE ONE.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: pray for Christian unity. Settle, and breathe. Bring to mind a church that isn't yours, or isn't the kind you know best. A cathedral, a storefront chapel, an Orthodox church with icons, a house church, a church in another country. Picture the people there this week: singing, arguing about the budget, bringing casseroles. If you pray, you can say his words for them and for your own: that they all may be one. If you don't, simply hold them in goodwill for a few breaths. The bell holds the time.
Ecumenism. The modern movement toward Christian unity that this prayer, that they may all be one, became a seed for.
Your line: that they may be one. Today, say one generous thing about a Christian tradition that isn't the one you know best. Day six hundred forty-one.

howItsDone: Churches in many places keep a yearly Week of Prayer for Christian Unity, often in January, when Catholic, Orthodox and Protestant Christians pray together, often using the words of John 17:21.

original.note: Greek: that all may be one. in Latin, ut omnes unum sint.

trapdoor: what you thought: a nice wish that people get along.
what it means: a prayer for everyone who would ever believe, modeled on the bond of Father and Son, aimed at the watching world.
what a scholar hears: hen, one, is neuter, not 'one person', and the verse never says what shape the oneness takes, which is part of why churches still read it differently.

notes: East–West schism dated to the eleventh century (usually 1054); 'thousands of separate church bodies' is a common estimate and varies by definition. Confirm.
Ut Unum Sint, encyclical of John Paul II, 25 May 1995. Confirm.
Three views of unity given without ranking. Keeper should check fairness.
Week of Prayer for Christian Unity, traditionally 18–25 January in the northern hemisphere. Confirm.
Trapdoor: hen (neuter) in 17:21; the inference about 'oneness of life' is interpretive. Confirm or soften.
